Every reward-to-risk ratio, stop-ATR multiple, break-even and expectancy in this report was recomputed from entry, target and downside against live ATR(14) at synthesis and matched the research figures exactly. ALL EIGHT IDEAS ARE LONG, and the report also closes two shorts and withdraws a third, so the book goes from mixed to one-sided on a midterm election day three days before a payroll print whose prior was 29K. That is a deliberate consequence of the evidence, not an oversight, and it is the single thing most likely to make today's report wrong together rather than wrong one idea at a time. SIX OF EIGHT RESOLVE ON AN EARNINGS PRINT INSIDE SIX SESSIONS: PFE today 2026-11-03, CVS and KHC on 11-04, CELH on 11-05, VST and ELAN on 11-06, ONON on 11-10. Six different sectors, so it is not one bet with extra steps — but it is one week, and the book is dense with event risk rather than spread. Correlation stands at the cap and not over it on two axes, and one of those counts is corrected here: consumer-adjacent is KHC, CELH and ONON (three); healthcare-adjacent is CVS, ELAN and PFE (three). The research notes recorded healthcare as two, a count made at 06:34 before PFE was added at 06:36 — three is the right number and it is exactly at the cap. XLE'S RATIO AND STOP ARE BOTH ARTIFACTS OF IT BEING AN AMENDMENT, read this before anyone 'fixes' it: the 66.50 stop sits ABOVE the 63.90 fill, so the 2.54:1 the validator computes from abs(entry-stop) describes a 2.60-point loss that cannot happen — what is actually at stake is 0.75 points of a 3.35-point unrealised gain. The same arithmetic makes the stop read 1.69 ATR against the 1.8 floor for an ETF swing and it will fail check_stop_distance, because the validator measures from the recorded fill, which is the right rule for a new entry and the wrong one for a protective trail 0.49 ATR BELOW the market. DO NOT WIDEN THE 66.50 STOP TO CLEAR THE FLOOR — that is the KRE mistake running backwards, buying a passing grade by making the trade worse. Demotion to the watchlist is the lesser error and is the correct outcome. INSIDER OPEN-MARKET BUYING IS THE SPINE OF THIS REPORT and was promoted from a confirmation to the primary screen because the track record argued for it: PFE (3 buyers including CEO Bourla, $2.96M), ELAN (7 distinct buyers, $1.67M, zero sales), CELH (4 buyers including CEO Fieldly, $2.55M, zero sales), ONON (all three co-founders, $10.58M), KHC (CEO Cahillane, $5.0M), VST (CEO Burke, $1.17M). Its absence is what killed AAP and BCC. HOW THE TRACK RECORD CHANGED THE BAR: 3/32 hit target (9%), avg -5.7%, with stocks 1/21 (5%) and conviction-3 ideas 1/19 (5%). n=32 is past the ~15-trade noise line, so it was treated as signal — no conviction-3 idea was published as a NEW idea today (the only 3 in the book is the XLE amendment), and JETS, the day's most obvious trade, was rejected explicitly because its evidence topped out at two distinct kinds. RATIOS ARE NOT CLUSTERED AT THE FLOOR — they run 2.05, 2.33, 2.40, 2.54, 2.83, 2.93, 3.44, 5.54, which is a spread rather than the signature of targets fitted to clear a bar. The one exception is VST at 2.05, and it is published only because wait is true and entry is conditioned on 130 holding the print. Conviction equals the count of distinct evidence kinds on every idea with nothing rounded up; four candidates were deliberately held at 4 rather than 5 because counter_argument_answered did not honestly hold — for VST and CELH the print is being waited for rather than the bear case answered, and for ELAN and ONON the strongest objection (Elanco's leverage and generic exposure, On's exposure to a constrained premium consumer) could not be researched this run. DATA GAPS AND FAILED SOURCES. (1) The most consequential, and an engineering finding rather than a research one: market_data.py earnings has a TWO-DAY BLIND SPOT at the front of its window — it returned no rows dated 2026-11-03 or 2026-11-04 at all. THREE PRINTS ON THE OPEN BOOK sat inside it — PFE today, CVS and KHC tomorrow — and all three were caught only by hand. Anything else reporting today or tomorrow may have been missed. (2) market_data.py macro produced nothing: two timeouts at 120s and 180s, zero output. No FRED series, no VIX and no DXY this run, so those levels are null below and the macro picture is reconstructed from ETF proxies, Kalshi prices and the web, and is labelled that way throughout. (3) market_data.py implied returns HTTP 401 from yahoo-options, so no idea carries an options-implied move and none of the six earnings-driven ideas could be checked against what the straddle prices. (4) market_data.py short times out on api.nasdaq.com, so there is no short-interest or days-to-cover reading on anything, including the two shorts being closed. (5) market_data.py events samples only the first 200 open Kalshi markets and cannot find a named series; worked around by calling the Kalshi per-market endpoint directly, since the list endpoint returns null prices. (6) Robinhood's prediction-markets page came back truncated, so the Commodities category could not be enumerated and NO WTI CONTRACT WAS RECOMMENDED on the day of a 7.4% crude move — universe.md says verify, not infer. (7) AAP's earnings date could not be reconciled between Finnhub (11-05) and stockanalysis.com (10-29) and the idea was dropped for that reason alone; PYPL's next earnings date could not be found at all, and ABT's and STLD's could not be confirmed either way — recorded as unknown, not as none. WHY EIGHT: eight is the honest count, not a shortfall and not a target. The day had one dominant macro event and a dense earnings week, and these are the ideas where fetched insider data, a verified earnings date and a real price level lined up. JETS, AAP, UAA, WIX, ENOV and XLY were each rejected for a specific reason recorded in notes.md. The gas-price contract KXAAAGASMAX-26DEC31-4.60 is the one this run believes is genuinely mispriced — the NO at 0.76 against an 8-12% estimate of YES is +18.4% over 59 days — and it is NOT published, because a favourite at 0.76 risks 76 to make 24, which is 0.32:1 and can never clear a 2.0 floor. It is on the watchlist with the numbers rather than quietly dropped, and no synthetic 64c stop was invented to manufacture a passing ratio. Prices throughout are the 2026-11-02 close, taken pre-open with US equities shut — that is a closed market, not stale data; quotes were re-fetched at synthesis and every one matched research to the cent. RED TEAM (phase 2c). Cut two of eight, downgraded two, corrected one ratio; six remain. VST cut: the 2.05:1 clears the floor only because the stop was walked in 112.14 -> 114.00 -> 117.00 across three republications at an unchanged 132.00 entry while the target was cut 171.72 -> 162.70; at its originally published stop the ratio is 1.55:1 and at a defensible 2.5 ATR stop 1.69:1, both under the floor, so it never cleared it. XLE cut as synthesis expected, but all three of its failures are artifacts rather than defects and ONE ITEM NEEDS A HUMAN: merge_report reads recommendations only, so the 66.50 trail will not reach the tracker and open_positions keeps a 60.80 stop 9.7% below the market — set it by hand. Its scale plan's claim that the stop was raised on 2026-11-02 is also false; that report held only RTX and XLU. PFE's ratio corrected 5.54 -> 3.62 by returning the bear-case anchor to 23.62: eleven prior publications at the identical 27.60 entry and 42.00 target anchored between 23.00 and 24.40, including 23.62 three days ago, and 25.00 lifted the ratio 53% with nothing else moved, which is the KRE failure mode and not new work. KHC lowered 5 -> 4: its fourth evidence kind claims the beat streak answers the declining-volumes bear case, which its own key_risk denies on the same page and which the report refuses on PFE as cost control against declining revenue. CVS lowered 4 -> 3: the positioning evidence counted toward its score argues against the direction in its own words (zero insider buys, $359.0M of sales, "no officer has bought this de-rating at any price"), and absent insider buying is the screen that killed AAP and BCC today. NOT CUT, and said plainly rather than dressed up as diligence: CELH and ONON both survive the stop-widening recheck with room (2.85:1 and 2.22:1 at a 2.5 ATR stop), both anchor entry to a dated insider purchase band rather than to a discount off the last price, and both carry intermediate trims at real resistance, which is the right answer to the target_feasibility warnings they share with the rest of the book. ELAN kept: its spread FAIL is an empty pre-market book, not a transaction cost — bid 21.75 against ask 26.59 on a $12B name at 06:45 with the market shut — and check_spread reads market_session in the same breath without using it, so phase 2d may yet demote ELAN on an artifact; if it does, that is the reason. CVS at 2.40%, ONON at 2.26% and CELH at 2.30% are the same artifact at smaller scale. TWO ENGINEERING FINDINGS, both correcting what this report says above. (1) The earnings calendar has NO front blind spot — the diagnosis above is wrong and the open worry it leaves ("anything else reporting today or tomorrow may have been missed") is closable. Finnhub caps the response near 1500 rows and the truncation drops the FRONT of the window, so asking for more days returns fewer early days: --days 14 starts 2026-11-08, --days 12 starts 11-05, and --days 2, 3 and 5 all start 11-03 and carry 295 reporters today and 463 tomorrow. Research asked for 12 days, which is exactly why PFE, CVS and KHC had to be found by hand. Query narrow to see the front. Re-checked on the untruncated calendar, NOTHING WAS MISSED: the only live or pending positions reporting through 11-08 are PFE today, CVS and KHC tomorrow and VST on 11-06, all four of which were caught. It also settles three dates this report recorded as unknown — ABT, PYPL and STLD have no print between 11-03 and 11-17 — and flags two pending orders that do: OXY on 11-09 and SMMT on 11-11. (2) check_sources probes with HEAD and treats a 404 as evidence a source was invented, but a host may 404 a HEAD and serve a GET, which is what cost XLE a FAIL on a live page. Both are worth a test in tests/. RED TEAM ADDENDUM, and it retires the scariest-looking line in this report. The earnings_date warning carried by every single surviving idea is a FALSE NEGATIVE in all six cases, from the same truncation as finding (1): check_earnings_date calls md.earnings(45), and a 45-day request truncates the front of the window hardest of all, so the check never sees the near-dated region that is the only place a claimed catalyst date could be verified. Queried narrow instead, EVERY CLAIMED DATE IS CONFIRMED on Finnhub's own calendar — PFE 2026-11-03, CVS and KHC 11-04, CELH 11-05, ELAN 11-06, ONON 11-10. Read "not on the fetched calendar" as "the calendar was asked the wrong question", and treat all six dates as firm rather than near-firm. The fix is a narrow window in fetch_context, and it needs a test in tests/ that asserts a date three sessions out is actually found. Validation demoted 1 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 5 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

That number is the setup: the SMA20 is 34.135 and Monday's session low was 34.18, so the founders' average, the 20-day average and the most recent test of support are the same price to within seven cents, and the stock closed 35.52 just under the 36.08 resistance.
recommendations.key_risk: ONON sells premium-priced footwear into a US consumer that other retailers are describing as constrained — AAP cited tighter household budgets for a declining DIY business in the same quarter — and the beat streak has already flattened: Q2 2026 EPS came in at 0.35 against 0.3439, a +1.8% surprise, after +51.5%, +20.9% and +87.4%. recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that founder buying in a company they control is not an independent signal — they were buying at 36.75 and the stock went to 26.37, so their timing has already been wrong once by 28%, and averaging down is what a committed owner does regardless of the setup. That is fair, and it is why the idea is anchored on the price confluence rather than on the signal alone: 34.14 is where their money is, where the 20-day average is, and where Monday actually found a bid. The stop at 31.20 sits below the 27 October low of 31.28, so being wrong costs 2.31 ATR and not a thesis.

RED TEAM: the conviction-5 score was withdrawn to 4.
